title: Open Files and Rooks
description: Rooks crave open files. Learn how to seize and exploit open and half-open files, double rooks, and invade the seventh rank.

sections.title: Seizing the Open File
sections.content: A file with no pawns is an open file — a highway for rooks. The side that controls it first can invade the enemy position. Place a rook on the file and contest control.

positions.commentary: The d-file is open. Whoever controls it dominates. White should contest or seize the file and look to penetrate to the seventh or eighth rank.

sections.title: The Seventh Rank
sections.content: A rook on the seventh rank (the enemy's second) attacks pawns and traps the king. Two rooks on the seventh — "pigs on the seventh" — are often decisive.

positions.commentary: A rook on the seventh rank devours pawns and cuts off the enemy king. This is one of the most powerful rook placements in chess.

exercises.title: Claim the File
exercises.description: White to play. Contest the open d-file with your rook.
hints: Put the rook on the open file
